gloss: be strong, prevail; man, strong one; mighty, warrior; might
summary: To be stronger and so to prevail: waters that rise over the mountains, Israel over Amalek while Moses' hands are raised, an enemy over the desolate. Its nouns name the one who has that strength: גֶּבֶר is a man, the grown male as against women and children, and above all the mortal man before God who dies and is laid low; גִּבּוֹר is the mighty one, the warrior, and Yahweh himself, “mighty in battle”; גְּבוּרָה is might, and in the plural mighty deeds, God's above all. Scripture's constant lesson in these words is that “not by strength shall a man prevail” (1Sa 2:9).

words.summary: The commonest word of the root, about 160 times: the strong man of war, a champion, a man of valour or of substance, and Yahweh as the mighty one who fights and saves. Its opposite is the weak (חַלָּשׁ, Jol 4:10), and it stands beside the swift and the man of war.

senses.gloss: warrior, mighty man of war, champion
senses.definition: A man strong in battle: a fighting man, one of a king's picked warriors, or the champion who fights for a whole army.

evidence.note: Hushai on David's men: “they are גִּבֹּרִים, and bitter of soul like a bear robbed of her cubs … your father is a man of war.”
When Goliath fell, “the Philistines saw that their גִּבּוֹר was dead”: their champion.
“Beat your ploughshares into swords … let the weak (הַחַלָּשׁ) say, I am a גִּבּוֹר.”
“Let not the swift flee, nor the גִּבּוֹר escape.”
“The strong shall not hold his strength, nor shall the גִּבּוֹר deliver himself.”
First among the stays of Jerusalem: “גִּבּוֹר and man of war.”
“These are the names of the גִּבֹּרִים whom David had.”
“The race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the גִּבּוֹרִים.”
“Shall the prey be taken from the גִּבּוֹר? … even the captives of the גִּבּוֹר shall be taken.”
“As arrows in the hand of a גִּבּוֹר, so are the sons of youth.”
“A גִּבּוֹר is not delivered by much strength.”

senses.gloss: man of valour; man of substance (גִּבּוֹר חַיִל)
senses.definition: With חַיִל “strength, wealth”: a man of standing, whether for valour in war or for wealth and position; the context decides which.

evidence.note: The angel to Gideon: “Yahweh is with you, גִּבּוֹר הֶחָיִל.”
Jephthah the Gileadite “was a גִּבּוֹר חַיִל”.
Boaz, “a man גִּבּוֹר חַיִל of the family of Elimelech”: a man of substance.
Menahem exacted the silver “from all the גִּבּוֹרֵי הַחַיִל, fifty shekels of silver from each man”: men of wealth.
Kish, Saul's father, “a גִּבּוֹר חָיִל”.
Jeroboam, “a גִּבּוֹר חַיִל”, put in charge of the forced labour of the house of Joseph.

senses.definition: Strong or great beyond others in some respect: a hunter, a lion among beasts, the sun on its course, angels in strength; and, in irony, men mighty at drinking wine.

evidence.note: Nimrod “began to be a גִּבֹּר in the earth; he was a גִּבֹּר hunter before Yahweh”.
“The same were the גִּבֹּרִים which were of old, men of renown.”
“The lion, which is גִּבּוֹר among beasts, and turns not back from any.”
The sun “rejoices as a גִּבּוֹר to run his course”.
His angels, “גִּבֹּרֵי כֹחַ, that do his word, hearkening to the voice of his word”.
“Woe to those who are גִּבּוֹרִים to drink wine.”
Of the man who fears Yahweh: “his seed shall be גִּבּוֹר in the land.”
“Better is he who is slow to anger than a גִּבּוֹר, and he who rules his spirit than he who takes a city.”
“Why do you boast in evil, O הַגִּבּוֹר?”

senses.definition: Of Yahweh: mighty in battle, the warrior who goes out against his enemies and the mighty one who saves; in the titles “the great, the mighty and the terrible God” and “mighty God”.

evidence.note: “Yahweh your God … the great God, הַגִּבֹּר, and the terrible, who regards not persons.”
“Who is this King of glory? Yahweh strong and גִּבּוֹר, Yahweh גִּבּוֹר in battle.”
“Yahweh shall go forth as a גִּבּוֹר, as a man of war he shall stir up zeal.”
“Yahweh your God in your midst is a גִּבּוֹר; he will save.”
“Yahweh is with me as a terrible גִּבּוֹר.”
“The great, the גִּבּוֹר God, Yahweh of hosts is his name.”
“The Lord awoke as one asleep, like a גִּבּוֹר shouting because of wine.”
“A remnant shall return, the remnant of Jacob, to אֵל גִּבּוֹר”, that is, to “Yahweh the Holy One of Israel” (Isa 10:20).
Among the names of the child born, the son given: אֵל גִּבּוֹר.

senses.definition: Of the king whom Yahweh anoints: the mighty one on whom Yahweh lays help, who girds on his sword.

evidence.note: “I have laid help upon a גִּבּוֹר; I have exalted one chosen out of the people. I have found David my servant; with my holy oil I have anointed him.”
“Gird your sword upon your thigh, O גִּבּוֹר, your glory and your majesty.”

evidence.locator: Zep.3.17, גִּבּוֹר יוֹשִׁיעַ → δυνατὸς σώσει; δυνατός renders גִּבּוֹר ×58

evidence.note: Mary: “he who is mighty (ὁ δυνατός) has done great things for me, and holy is his name”: God as the גִּבּוֹר who saves (Zep 3:17).

parallels.note: “Man of war”, the fixed partner of גִּבּוֹר.
The swift, set beside the mighty as those who might escape or win.

opposites.note: The weak, who will say “I am a גִּבּוֹר”.

phrases.gloss: mighty man of valour; man of substance

words.summary: A man, chiefly in poetry: the grown male set apart from women and little ones, and the single man in his weakness and mortality before God. It is the man of the root's strength, but scripture uses it most where that strength fails: the man who dies, who is cursed when he trusts in man, blessed when he trusts in Yahweh.

senses.gloss: man, male (as against women and children)
senses.definition: The grown men of a people or household, counted apart from women and children, and the man as distinct from the woman.

evidence.note: “About six hundred thousand on foot, הַגְּבָרִים, besides little ones.”
Pharaoh: “Not so! Go now, הַגְּבָרִים, and serve Yahweh”: the men without the little ones (Exo 10:10).
“The thing of a גֶּבֶר shall not be on a woman, nor shall a גֶּבֶר put on a woman's garment.”
“Ask whether a male (זָכָר) bears a child; why do I see every גֶּבֶר with his hands on his loins like a woman in labour?”
“Yahweh has created a new thing in the land: a female (נְקֵבָה) shall surround a גָּבֶר.”
“גְּבָרִים, men of war, and women and little ones and eunuchs.”
The household that Yahweh takes shall come near “by the men” (לַגְּבָרִים), man by man.
“The way of a גֶּבֶר with a young woman.”
“The night which said, A גָּבֶר is conceived.”

senses.definition: The individual man as God's creature: weak, mortal and accountable, whose steps are ordered by Yahweh, and who is blessed or cursed according to where he puts his trust.

evidence.note: “But גֶּבֶר dies and is laid low; man (אָדָם) gives up his breath, and where is he?”
“What גֶּבֶר shall live and not see death, shall deliver his soul from the hand of the grave?”
“If a גֶּבֶר dies, shall he live again? All the days of my service I will wait, until my change come.”
“Shall mortal man (אֱנוֹשׁ) be righteous before God? Shall a גֶּבֶר be pure before his maker?”
“Can a גֶּבֶר be profitable to God?”
“The steps of a גֶּבֶר are established by Yahweh.”
“The steps of a גֶּבֶר are from Yahweh; how then can man understand his way?”
“Cursed is the גֶּבֶר who trusts in man and makes flesh his arm.”
“Blessed is the גֶּבֶר who trusts in Yahweh.”
“Blessed is the גֶּבֶר who takes refuge in him.”
“Blessed is the גֶּבֶר whom you chasten, Yah.”
“I am the גֶּבֶר who has seen affliction by the rod of his wrath.”
“It is good for a גֶּבֶר that he bear the yoke in his youth.”
“I am like a גֶּבֶר who has no strength (אֱיָל)”: a man whose strength is gone.
Coniah: “a גֶּבֶר who shall not prosper in his days.”

senses.gloss: man (in his strength), man of standing
senses.definition: A man as one who has strength to stand and answer, or a man of note whose words are given as an oracle.

evidence.note: “Gird up now your loins like a גֶּבֶר; I will ask of you, and you shall answer me.”
“The oracle of David son of Jesse, the oracle of the גֶּבֶר who was raised up on high, the anointed of the God of Jacob.”
“The oracle of Balaam son of Beor, the oracle of the גֶּבֶר whose eye is opened.”
“Sword, awake against my shepherd, against the גֶּבֶר who is my fellow, says Yahweh of hosts; strike the shepherd.”
Jesus applies Zec 13:7 to himself: “I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered.”
“A proud גֶּבֶר, who does not stay at home.”

evidence.locator: Psa.34.9; Psa.40.5, אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר → μακάριος ἀνήρ; Job.38.3; Zec.13.7; ἀνήρ renders גֶּבֶר ×34

evidence.note: “Blessed is the man (μακάριος ἀνήρ) who endures trial”: the Psalms' אַשְׁרֵי הַגֶּבֶר; the Peshitta has גַּבְרָא.

parallels.note: Man, mankind: “גֶּבֶר dies … אָדָם gives up his breath.”

opposites.note: The woman, whose garment a גֶּבֶר must not put on.

phrases.gloss: blessed is the man (on the right path is the man)

words.summary: Might: the strength of a man, a horse or an army, the deeds of a king, and above all Yahweh's might and his mighty acts, which his people declare from generation to generation.

senses.definition: The bodily or warlike strength of a man, an army or a horse; the vigour of life.

evidence.note: Zebah and Zalmunna to Gideon: “Rise and fall on us, for as the man is, so is his גְּבוּרָה.”
“It is not the sound of the shout of גְּבוּרָה, nor the sound of the shout of weakness (חֲלוּשָׁה)”: the victors' shout, as against the defeated.
“He delights not in the גְּבוּרָה of the horse.”
“Have you given the horse גְּבוּרָה?”
“The days of our years are seventy years, and if by reason of גְּבוּרֹת, eighty years.”
“Your men shall fall by the sword, and your גְּבוּרָה in the war.”
“Counsel and גְּבוּרָה for war.”
“Let not the mighty man (הַגִּבּוֹר) glory in his גְּבוּרָה.”
“Wisdom is better than גְּבוּרָה.”
Princes who eat in due season, “for גְּבוּרָה and not for drunkenness”.
“Their course is evil, and their גְּבוּרָה is not right.”
“All his גְּבוּרָה … are they not written in the book of the chronicles?”: a king's might and exploits.

senses.definition: Yahweh's power, and in the plural the deeds that show it, by which he saves his people and makes his name known.

evidence.note: “What god is there in heaven or in earth who can do according to your works and according to your גְבוּרֹת?”
“One generation shall praise your works to another, and shall declare your גְּבוּרֹת.”
“They shall speak of your גְּבוּרָה, to make known to the sons of man his גְּבוּרֹת and the glorious majesty of his kingdom.”
“Praise him for his גְבוּרֹת.”
“He saved them for his name's sake, to make known his גְּבוּרָה.”
“I will make them know my hand and my גְבוּרָה, and they shall know that my name is Yahweh.”
“Save me, O God, by your name, and judge me by your גְבוּרָה.”
“You have an arm with גְּבוּרָה.”
“Who establishes the mountains by his strength, being girded with גְּבוּרָה.”
“Yours, Yahweh, is the greatness and the גְּבוּרָה and the glory … yours is the kingdom … in your hand is power and גְבוּרָה.”
The doxology “for yours is the kingdom and the power (δύναμις) and the glory”, the words of 1Ch 29:11.
“With him is wisdom and גְבוּרָה; he has counsel and understanding.”

senses.definition: Might as God's gift, given with wisdom and counsel by his spirit to the one who judges and to the prophet.

evidence.note: On the shoot from Jesse: “the spirit of Yahweh shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and גְבוּרָה.”
“I am full of power by the spirit of Yahweh, and of judgment and of גְבוּרָה, to declare to Jacob his transgression.”
Wisdom: “I am understanding; I have גְבוּרָה.”
Yahweh will be “for גְבוּרָה to those who turn back the battle at the gate”.

evidence.locator: 1Ch.29.11, וְהַגְּבוּרָה → καὶ ἡ δύναμις; δύναμις renders גְּבוּרָה ×11

evidence.note: “Yours is the kingdom and the power (ἡ δύναμις) and the glory”: David's words in 1Ch 29:11.

parallels.note: Wisdom, set beside might, and above it.

words.gloss: be strong, prevail; (piel) strengthen; (hiphil) make strong, confirm; (hithpael) show oneself mighty, behave proudly
words.summary: Twenty-five times. In the qal it is to be stronger than something and so get the upper hand: waters over the earth, one army over another, iniquities over a man, Yahweh's steadfast love over those who fear him.

senses.definition: To be stronger than an opponent and overcome: in battle, of an enemy, of iniquities, of a brother over his brothers.

evidence.note: “When Moses held up his hand, Israel וְגָבַר; and when he let down his hand, Amalek וְגָבַר.”
“For not by strength shall a man יִגְבַּר.”
“The men גָבְרוּ against us and came out to us into the field.”
“My sons are desolate, because the enemy גָבַר.”
“Iniquities גָּבְרוּ against me; as for our transgressions, you will cover them.”
“Judah גָּבַר over his brothers, and from him came the prince.”
“They are not valiant (גָבְרוּ) for faithfulness in the land.”

senses.gloss: be strong, mighty; be greater, rise above
senses.definition: To be strong or grow mighty; to be greater than, rise over: waters over the mountains, blessings over blessings, Yahweh's steadfast love over his people.

evidence.note: “The waters וַיִּגְבְּרוּ and increased greatly on the earth … fifteen cubits upward did the waters גָּבְרוּ, and the mountains were covered.”
Saul and Jonathan: “they were swifter than eagles, they גָּבֵרוּ more than lions.”
“The blessings of your father גָּבְרוּ above the blessings of my progenitors.”
“Why do the wicked live, become old, גָּבְרוּ in power?”
“As the heavens are high above the earth, גָּבַר his steadfast love toward those who fear him.”
“For his steadfast love גָּבַר over us.”

senses.definition: To make strong; with חֲיָלִים, to put more strength into a task.

evidence.note: “וְגִבַּרְתִּי the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph.”
“וְגִבַּרְתִּים in Yahweh, and they shall walk up and down in his name.”
“If the iron is blunt … then he must יְגַבֵּר strength (חֲיָלִים).”

senses.definition: To make something strong or to prevail by it: by the tongue, or by making a covenant strong.

evidence.note: “Who have said, With our tongue נַגְבִּיר; our lips are our own; who is lord over us?”
“וְהִגְבִּיר a covenant with many for one seven.”

senses.definition: To act the mighty one: of Yahweh over his enemies, and of a man setting himself up against God.

evidence.note: “Yahweh shall go forth as a גִּבּוֹר … against his enemies יִתְגַּבָּר.”
“He stretched out his hand against God, and against Shaddai יִתְגַּבָּר.”
“He shows them their work and their transgressions, that they יִתְגַּבָּרוּ.”

words.summary: Twice, both in Isaac's blessing of Jacob: the one who is master over his brothers.

senses.definition: One set over others, who serve him.

evidence.note: “Let peoples serve you … be גְבִיר over your brothers, and let your mother's sons bow down to you.”
“I have made him גְּבִיר over you, and all his brothers I have given to him for servants.”

words.summary: The feminine of גְּבִיר: the mistress whom a maidservant serves, and Babylon's boast to be mistress of kingdoms. It shares no cognate of its own; its meaning is the master's.

senses.definition: The woman a maidservant serves.

evidence.note: When Hagar conceived, “her גְּבִרְתָּהּ was despised in her eyes”.
“I flee from the face of my גְּבִרְתִּי Sarai.”
“As the eyes of servants to the hand of their masters, as the eyes of a maidservant to the hand of her גְּבִרְתָּהּ, so our eyes are to Yahweh our God.”

senses.definition: Of Babylon, the city that ruled the nations.

evidence.note: “You shall no more be called גְּבֶרֶת of kingdoms.”
“You said, I shall be גְבֶרֶת for ever.”

words.summary: The lady of the royal house: in Judah the king's mother, who held a recognised rank, and in Egypt Pharaoh's queen.

senses.definition: The woman of first rank at court: the king's mother in Judah, a queen in Egypt.

evidence.note: Asa removed Maacah his mother “from being גְּבִירָה, because she had made an abomination for Asherah”.
“Say to the king and to the גְּבִירָה, Humble yourselves, sit down.”
“Jeconiah the king and the גְּבִירָה.”
“The sons of the king and the sons of the גְּבִירָה.”
“Tahpenes the גְּבִירָה”, Pharaoh's wife.

words.summary: Biblical Aramaic's word for a man, in Daniel and Ezra, chiefly in the plural, “these men”. BDB's key also counts Hebrew Psa 18:26 (גְּבַר תָּמִים), the construct of גֶּבֶר, by spelling.

senses.definition: A man, a person; in the plural, men.

evidence.note: “I have found a גְּבַר of the sons of the captivity of Judah.”
“I see four גֻּבְרִין loose, walking in the midst of the fire.”
“There is a גְּבַר in your kingdom in whom is the spirit of the holy gods.”

words.summary: Once in Biblical Aramaic, in גִּבָּרֵי־חַיִל, the Aramaic of Hebrew גִּבּוֹרֵי חַיִל.

senses.definition: A strong man of war.

evidence.note: He commanded “גִּבָּרֵי־חַיִל who were in his army” to bind Shadrach, Meshach and Abed-nego.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ordinary word for a man, for Greek ἀνήρ and ἄνθρωπος, and for a husband.

senses.definition: A man, a male person.

evidence.note: “Jesus the Nazarene, a גַּבְרָא (ἄνδρα) approved of God among you by mighty works and wonders.”
God “will judge the world in righteousness by the גַּבְרָא (ἀνδρί) whom he has appointed”.
“After me comes a גַּבְרָא who was before me.”
“A wise גַּבְרָא who built his house on the rock.”
“Blessed is the גַּבְרָא who endures trial.”
“To a perfect גַּבְרָא, to the measure of the stature of the fulness of Christ.”

senses.definition: A woman's husband.

evidence.note: “Joseph the גַּבְרָא of Mary, of whom was born Jesus.”
The woman is bound by the law to her living husband.
“The head of every man is Christ, and the head of the woman is the man.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's word for Greek τέρας, “wonder”, always beside “signs”: the mighty deeds of God, as Hebrew גְבוּרֹת.

senses.definition: A wonder done by God's power, named with signs and mighty works.

evidence.note: Peter quoting Joel 3:3: “I will give גַּבְרוּתָא (τέρατα) in the heaven above, and signs on the earth below.”
Jesus approved of God “by mighty works and גַּבְרוּתָא and signs”.
Moses brought Israel out “having done גַּבְרוּתָא and signs in Egypt”.

words.gloss: (ethpaal) act like a man, be courageous
words.summary: Once in the Peshitta, the ethpaal for Greek ἀνδρίζομαι: to be a man, show manly courage.

stems.gloss: act like a man, be courageous

senses.definition: To show the strength and courage of a man.

evidence.note: “Watch, stand fast in the faith, אֶתְגַּבַּרוּ (ἀνδρίζεσθε), be strong.”

cognates.gloss: man; young man; courageous man; king; slave, servant
cognates.note: The noun of the same pattern as גֶּבֶר, meaning a man, and also a king (as גְּבִיר) or a servant. Arabic j answers to Hebrew ג.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 374, art. جبر, جَبْرٌ (n4937)
evidence.note: “A king; … and a slave, or servant: … and a man: … and a young man: and [a] courageous [man].”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 374, art. جبر, جَبْرَئِيلُ (n4946)
evidence.note: Gabriel's name explained from جَبْرٌ “man” or “servant” and إِيلٌ “God”.

evidence.locator: Proto-West Semitic *gabr-
evidence.note: “Man”, with Arabic جَبْر, Aramaic גַּבְרָא, Ge'ez ገብር and Hebrew גֶּבֶר among its descendants.

cognates.gloss: overbearing, tyrant; mighty; (of God) the Compeller, the Supreme; tall (palm)
cognates.note: The same pattern as גִּבּוֹר (*gabbār): the man who is mighty and lords it over others, and, of God, the Supreme. Lane's tropical senses (Orion as a crowned king, a palm too tall to reach) keep the sense of what is great beyond others.

evidence.locator: Book I, pp. 374–375, art. جبر, جَبَّارٌ (n4956)
evidence.note: “One who magnifies himself … imperious, or domineering, by absolute force and power; overbearing; tyrannical; a tyrant … الجَبَّار [A name of] God … the Supreme; the High above his creatures.”

evidence.locator: Proto-West Semitic *gabbār-
evidence.note: “Strong man, hero”, with Arabic جَبَّار, Aramaic גַּבָּרָא, Ge'ez ገባር and Hebrew גִּבּוֹר.

cognates.gloss: set (a bone), restore; compel, constrain; (V) magnify oneself, behave proudly
cognates.note: The verb: to compel another, to overpower him, as the qal's prevailing; and form V, “he magnified himself; behaved proudly”, as the hithpael of Job 15:25 and 36:9. The bone-setting and restoring senses are Arabic's own development and have no Hebrew counterpart.

doctrine.statement: The word for man as the strong one is the word scripture uses for his dying: “גֶּבֶר dies and is laid low; man gives up his breath, and where is he?” (Job 14:10); “what גֶּבֶר shall live and not see death, shall deliver his soul from the hand of the grave?” (Psa 89:49). Job says the man who lies down does not rise “till the heavens be no more”, and asks, “If a גֶּבֶר dies, shall he live? All the days of my service I will wait, until my change (חֲלִיפָתִי) come. You will call, and I will answer you” (Job 14:12–15). Paul speaks of the same waiting ended: “we shall all be changed … the dead shall be raised incorruptible” (1Co 15:51–52). From the verses: a man's strength does not keep him from death or bring him out of the grave; his hope of living again is that God will call him back at the resurrection.

Hannah sang, “not by strength shall a man prevail (יִגְבַּר)” (1Sa 2:9); a psalm says, “a mighty man (גִּבּוֹר) is not delivered by much strength” (Psa 33:16), and another, “he delights not in the strength (גְּבוּרַת) of the horse … Yahweh takes pleasure in those who fear him” (Psa 147:10–11). Through Jeremiah Yahweh says, “let not the mighty man glory in his might … but let him who glories glory in this, that he understands and knows me” (Jer 9:22–23), which Paul sums up, “he who glories, let him glory in the Lord” (1Co 1:31); and “cursed is the גֶּבֶר who trusts in man … blessed is the גֶּבֶר who trusts in Yahweh” (Jer 17:5, 7). The strengthening that saves is Yahweh's: “I will strengthen (וְגִבַּרְתִּי) the house of Judah … I will strengthen them in Yahweh” (Zec 10:6, 12). From the verses: man's might, which these words name, is never the ground of victory or of boasting; the one who prevails is the one Yahweh strengthens.

Isaiah names the child born and the son given to sit on David's throne, “Wonderful Counsellor, אֵל גִּבּוֹר, Father of eternity, Prince of peace” (Isa 9:5–6); the next chapter gives the title אֵל גִּבּוֹר to Yahweh, the Holy One of Israel, to whom the remnant returns (Isa 10:20–21). Scripture gives God's titles to those through whom he acts: Yahweh says of his angel, “my name is in him” (Exo 23:21); a psalm calls the anointed king גִּבּוֹר and אֱלֹהִים, and then says, “God, your God, has anointed you above your fellows” (Psa 45:4, 7–8), which Hebrews applies to the Son (Heb 1:8–9); Yahweh says, “I have laid help upon a גִּבּוֹר … I have found David my servant” (Psa 89:20–21). Jesus says, “I have come in my Father's name” (Jhn 5:43), and Paul that God “gave him the name which is above every name” (Php 2:9). From the verses: the son is born and given, anointed by his God, and bears the name אֵל גִּבּוֹר because the mighty God's name and power are given to him and work through him; he is not, by bearing it, Yahweh himself.

Yahweh says, “Sword, awake against my shepherd, against the גֶּבֶר who is my fellow (עֲמִיתִי), says Yahweh of hosts; strike the shepherd, and the sheep shall be scattered” (Zec 13:7). On the night he was betrayed Jesus said, “All of you will be offended because of me this night, for it is written, I will strike the shepherd, and the sheep of the flock will be scattered” (Mat 26:31; Mrk 14:27). Peter preached “Jesus the Nazarene, a man (ἄνδρα; the Peshitta's גַּבְרָא) approved of God among you … delivered by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God” (Act 2:22–23). From the verses: the shepherd whom Yahweh's own sword strikes is a man, a גֶּבֶר, whom Yahweh calls his associate; he was struck by God's purpose, and his death scattered the flock for a time.

note: Drafted 2026-11-18. Root key גבר (c.am.aa as the root heading). BDB keys: c.am.aa verb, c.am.ac גֶּבֶר, c.am.af גִּבּוֹר, c.am.ag גְּבוּרָה, c.am.ah גְּבִיר, c.am.ai גְּבִירָה, c.am.aj גְּבֶרֶת; Biblical Aramaic xc.ab.ab גְּבַר and xc.ab.ad גִּבָּר. Names in names/: c.am.ak Gabriel, c.am.ad Geber. c.am.ad, BDB's proper name Geber, counts 17 tokens by spelling, most of them the common noun (Deu 22:5; Jer 22:30; Job 14:14…); the name itself is only 1Ki 4:13, 19, and the key is put on the name entry for those. c.am.ab (a cross-reference to גֶּבֶר, no tokens) is left unclaimed. c.am.ae גִּבָּר (Ezr 2:20) is left out: TIPNR files it as a place (the Gibeon of Neh 7:25), and places get no name entries. Ezion-geber (Num 33:35; Deu 2:8; 1Ki 9:26…) is a place, its tokens counted by spelling under c.am.ac and c.am.ad. xc.ab.ab also counts Hebrew Psa 18:26 by spelling. Peshitta: SEDRA root 337, lexemes 504 גַּבְרָא (≈297 tokens, ἀνήρ ×153, ἄνθρωπος ×113), 505 גַּבְרוּתָא (Act 2:19, 22, 43; 4:30; 5:12; 7:36; 15:12; 2Co 12:12; τέρας ×7) and 506 the ethpaal verb (1Co 16:13); lexeme 507 Gabriel (root 338) is cited on the name entry. The brief's Greek loan candidate ἰσχυρός is not a loan (Thayer derives it from ἰσχύω and only lists the Hebrew it renders) and is not recorded; the Septuagint renders Isa 49:24 גִּבּוֹר by γίγας, so Luk 11:21–22 and Mat 12:29 (the strong man bound) have no Greek bridge to the word, though they echo Isa 49:24–25. Akkadian: Oracc gives only gabarû “copy, counterpart, rival”, not recorded; no Akkadian cognate of “man, strong” found. Ugaritic: no gbr in Segert's glossary or Fisher (the OCR hits are qbr “bury”). Ge'ez ገብር gäbr “servant” and ገባር gäbbar are named only in Wiktionary's Proto-West Semitic pages; Dillmann not consulted, so not recorded. Old South Arabic: Biella's gbr hits are qbr “grave” and are not relevant. Lane's جَبْرٌ has both “king” and “slave, servant”, which Lane's sources call contrary meanings; גְּבִיר is named with it for “king, master”. Open questions: (1) whether the rooster sense of Mishnaic גֶּבֶר bears on any verse (Pro 30:31 has another word, זַרְזִיר); (2) Dan 9:27 וְהִגְבִּיר בְּרִית is glossed “make strong, confirm” without deciding who confirms the covenant: check against the prophecy data; (3) Gen 6:4's גִּבֹּרִים left without comment on the sons of God; (4) the doctrine “mighty-god-name-of-the-son” should be checked against elah.json, which notes the same title at Isa 9:5 and 10:21.
